items.body:
Slice 4 of decision record 0004 (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/0004-scope-resolved-roots.md`, PR #957). Depends on slice 1 (#958) and slice 3 (#959); slice 2 not required. Related: #864 (the fleet `.mcpx.json` still carries `/home/user` absolute paths — this slice needs the config in its post-#864 shape, or must say why it proceeded anyway).

## What to do
- Flip `gopls-mcp-server` to `"scope": "worktree"` in the fleet config (the user-level config symlinked to this repo's `.mcpx.json`; identical server lists on both machines stay identical).
- This is deliberately last: flipping scopes before the spawn-cwd and initialize work landed would only multiply processes.

## Acceptance criteria (live proof, from nix#817/#819)
- [ ] With gopls at `"scope": "worktree"` behind the fixed spawn cwd and initialize root, `go_package_api` on a module path returns the module's real API promptly (the 2026-10-25 result — empty after 156 s — does not recur).
- [ ] The same proof passes for a caller in a linked worktree, rooted in that worktree, not just the main checkout.
- [ ] Two callers in different checkouts get distinct gopls instances, each rooted in its own checkout (visible in `mcpx status` root field from slice 1).

items.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#817 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

## Problem

mcpx scopes choose *which* process serves a caller, but nothing tells that process *where the caller is*.

Scope keys already resolve the caller's cwd to a git root: `internal/config/scope.go` (`CallContext`, `Scope.Key()`) yields `repo:<git-common-dir>` / `worktree:<top-level>` using the native git discovery in `internal/config/gitdiscover.go`. But instance spawn ignores that resolution: `internal/pool/pool.go` `dial()` builds `StdioOptions{Cwd: p.cfg.Cwd}` — the config's static string, verbatim — and `internal/mcpclient/stdio.go` sets `cmd.Dir = opts.Cwd`. A `repo`- or `worktree`-scoped server therefore still *runs* in the daemon's cwd.

Concrete casualty (observed live, 2026-10-25, fleet config of 16 servers): gopls is a workspace server whose workspace is its process cwd. Scoped per-checkout it would still run in the daemon's cwd, so it loads files ad hoc ("command-line-arguments" package) instead of as a module workspace session.

## Proposed smallest design

When a server's scope is `repo` or `worktree` **and** its config `cwd` is empty, spawn the instance with `Dir` = the resolved scope root (the common-dir's worktree / the checkout top-level) instead of the daemon's cwd.

This needs the scope resolution to hand the pool the root, not just the opaque key string: return the resolved root alongside the key from `Scope.Key()`, or recompute it via `locateGit` at spawn time. One branch in `pool.dial()`.

Explicit config `cwd` always wins — the scope root is only the default when `cwd` is unset.

## Why this order

This is step 1 of the per-project design note (2026-10-25). With it, `"mcpx": {"scope": "worktree"}` on gopls becomes a real per-project workspace server: one gopls per checkout, rooted in that checkout. Flipping scopes *before* this lands only multiplies processes for little gain, so config scope flips wait for this issue.

Related: #818 — the `${mcpx.root}` / `${mcpx.cwd}` substitution issue (companion, step 2) — and #819 — the initialize `rootUri`/`workspaceFolders` issue (step 3, builds on the root resolution here).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `worktree`-scoped server with no config `cwd` is spawned with its working directory set to the caller's checkout top-level; a `repo`-scoped one to the resolved worktree of the common dir.
- [ ] Two callers in different checkouts of the same repo get distinct `worktree`-scoped instances rooted in their own checkouts; `repo` scope keeps sharing one instance per common dir.
- [ ] An explicit config `cwd` overrides the scope root in all cases.
- [ ] `global`/`cwd:`/`session` and other scopes are unchanged.
- [ ] A `worktree`-scoped gopls answers a package-level query (e.g. `go_package_api` on a module path) with the module's real API instead of an empty result.
- [ ] Tests cover the spawn-cwd decision (scope root vs explicit cwd vs daemon cwd fallback).

items.body:
Slice 1 of decision record 0004 (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/0004-scope-resolved-roots.md`, PR #957). Design source: dezren39/nix#817 — this issue carries its acceptance criteria.

## What to build (spec §1, §2, §3, §6)
- `internal/config`: add `ResolvedScope{Key, Root, Degraded}` and `Scope.Resolve(ctx)`; `Scope.Key` becomes `Resolve(ctx).Key` — one resolution path. Root semantics per spec §1 (worktree → checkout top-level; repo → parent of the common dir only when its base is `.git`, else no root; cwd → canonical caller cwd; degraded repo/worktree → that cwd; global/session/psession/pid/call → no root).
- Plumbing: `Registry.keyFor` switches to `Resolve` and passes the ResolvedScope into `Pool.Acquire`; the pool stores the root on the Instance at creation and `startLane`/`dial()` read it from the instance (never re-resolved at redial — root is a pure function of the key).
- Spawn cwd (stdio only): config `cwd` when non-empty, else the resolved root when non-empty, else unset (daemon cwd, today's behavior).
- Observability: one spawn log line (server, key, root, cwd source: config/scope/daemon); `mcpx status` instance JSON gains `root`.

## Acceptance criteria (from nix#817, verbatim intent)
- [ ] A `worktree`-scoped server with no config `cwd` spawns with its working directory set to the caller's checkout top-level; a `repo`-scoped one to the resolved worktree of the common dir.
- [ ] Two callers in different checkouts of the same repo get distinct `worktree`-scoped instances rooted in their own checkouts; `repo` scope keeps sharing one instance per common dir.
- [ ] An explicit config `cwd` overrides the scope root in all cases.
- [ ] `global`/`cwd:`/`session` and other scopes are unchanged.
- [ ] Tests cover the spawn-cwd decision (scope root vs explicit cwd vs daemon fallback) as a pure function, plus degraded-root cases.

(The gopls live-proof criterion from nix#817 belongs to slice 4, which has the full stack.)
